items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: He’s an old friend and has never forgotten it, and I’ve never forgotten it.

ctx.x: We’ve heard it a number of times.

And I also learned an important lesson, there are only two kinds of music: good music and bad music. So I tried to play as much good music as I possibly could. And worked © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

my way up, you know, after the war, worked in night clubs, The Copa and Bill Millers of the era, owned by that mythical organization. And met some people who were very helpful and still are. Skitch Henderson for example, who was a conductor, at that time a piano player with Frank Sinatra. And I found myself a job at NBC because Skitch’s lady friend, Faye Emerson, who was a wonderful movie star and a funny, bright woman, a beautiful woman, and she was a friend of Mr. Sarnoff which was very helpful. So I found…

items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: I brought men like... Bob Rosengarden... Bob and—... Always. Yes. He’s the time salesman.

ctx.x: —how the philosophy changes. Now it’s the elite job in New York. But at that time, they really didn’t want a staff job either. It was strange. They didn’t know where to go or what to do. So I brought men like, well I could start with Doc Carl Severinsen. I took him from Charlie Barnet’s band, and Clark Terry from the Ellington band, Tommy Newsom was with the Navy band in Washington, Hymie Schertzer had been with the Goodman band, I mean I could go through the whole, Bobby Haggart of course of fame, the best bass…
I’ll tell him that. You actually referred to him as the Chairman of the Board of the Time Factory.
